subtopics.title: Compose arguments to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts, using valid reasoning and relevant and sufficient evidence

outcomes.text: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization and style are appropriate to task, purpose and audience.

Introduce precise, knowledgeable claim(s), establish the significance of the claim(s), distinguish the claim(s)from alternate or opposing claims and create an organization that logically sequences claim(s), counterclaims, reasons and evidence.

Develop claim(s) and opposing claims fairly and thoroughly, supplying the most relevant evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level, concerns, values and possible biases.

Use words, phrases and clauses as well as varied syntax to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion and clarify the relationships between claim(s) and reasons, between reasons and evidence and between claim(s) and opposing claims.
Establish and maintain a task appropriate writing style.
Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument presented.
